newsitem.title: UK: Stg holds back Premier Farnell profit.
newsitem.headline: Stg holds back Premier Farnell profit.

text.p: Anglo-American Electronic components distributor Premier Farnell Plc said on Monday its full-year profits were held back by the strong pound and a slowdown in demand for electronic components.
Lacklustre demand resulted in a sharply lower profit contribution of Farnell Electronic Services (FES), which was sold in January at a profit of 43.3 million stg.
Premier Farnell said it now has a better mix of businesses.

"Following the disposal of FES, the group now comprises higher margin, service-orientated businesses and is well placed both financially and operationally to succeed in the global markets we serve," chief executive Howard Poulson said.
The group earlier reported that pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose to 137.4 million stg from 75.5 million following the Premier acquisition a year ago.

But earnings per share fell 18 percent to 29.1 pence due to the pound strength, reduced FES results and lower growth in the base business. Extra financing costs resulting from the Premier buy also weighed on the results.
The profits for the year to February 2 were released after Premier Farnell warned in January that results would be hit by weak market conditions, especially in its volume distribution business.
The group said on Monday it saw little change in the electronic components markets, although there were some "speculative" signs of improvements for some manufacturers.
Sales of Premier Farnell's British and US catalogue distributing companies were showing slow but consistent improvement, the firm said.
Premier Farnell reiterated that the integration of Premier was progressing successfully.
